challenges.title: React Hooks: useState and Functional Components
description: Modern React (since v16.8) uses hooks instead of class components. In 2026, all new React code is written with functional components and hooks.
useState is the most fundamental hook — it gives a functional component its own local state:

// Modern React with useState import React, { useState } from 'react'; function Counter() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); // initial value = 0 return ( <div> <p>Count: {count}</p> <button onClick={() => setCount(count + 1)}>Increment</button> <button onClick={() => setCount(count - 1)}>Decrement</button> </div> ); }
useState returns an array with two elements: the current state value and a setter function. Calling the setter triggers a re-render with the new value.
Hooks follow two rules: (1) only call hooks at the top level (not inside loops/conditions), and (2) only call hooks from React functions.
Instructions

Implement a createState factory function that mimics the behavior of React's useState. It takes an initial value and returns an array [getValue, setValue] where getValue() returns current state and setValue(newVal) updates it. This simulates how React tracks state internally.
tests: var pair = createState(0); var get = pair[0]; var set = pair[1]; assert(get() === 0, 'message: Initial value should be 0.');
set(5); assert(get() === 5, 'message: After setValue(5), getValue() should return 5.');
set(set(get() + 1)); assert(get() !== undefined, 'message: getValue() should always return the current state.');
var pair2 = createState('hello'); assert(pair2[0]() === 'hello', 'message: Should work with string initial values.');

challenges.title: React Hooks: useEffect and Side Effects
description: useEffect is React's hook for managing side effects — anything that reaches outside the component: data fetching, subscriptions, timers, DOM manipulation, and API calls.

import React, { useState, useEffect } from 'react'; function UserProfile({ userId }) { const [user, setUser] = useState(null); const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true); useEffect(() => { // Runs after every render where userId changed setLoading(true); fetch(`/api/users/${userId}`) .then(r => r.json()) .then(data => { setUser(data); setLoading(false); }); // Cleanup function (like componentWillUnmount) return () => { /* cancel fetch if needed */ }; }, [userId]); // dependency array — re-run only when userId changes if (loading) return <p>Loading...</p>; return <h1>{user.name}</h1>; }
The dependency array controls when the effect runs: empty [] = run once on mount, [dep1, dep2] = run when those values change, no array = run after every render.
Instructions

Write a function createEffect that mimics the basic behavior of useEffect: it takes an effect function and a deps array. Calling runEffect() should execute the effect only if the deps have changed since the last run. Return the last cleanup function if deps haven't changed.
challengeSeed: // Check if deps changed (use JSON.stringify for comparison)
var depsChanged = prevDeps === null || JSON.stringify(prevDeps) !== JSON.stringify(deps);
// run effect, store any cleanup it returns
tests: var ran = 0; var run = createEffect(function() { ran++; }, [1, 2]); run(); assert(ran === 1, 'message: Effect should run on first call.');
run(); assert(ran === 1, 'message: Effect should NOT run again when deps are the same.');

var ran2 = 0; var deps = [1]; var run2 = createEffect(function() { ran2++; }, deps); run2(); deps[0] = 2; run2 = createEffect(function() { ran2++; }, deps); run2(); assert(ran2 === 2, 'message: Effect should run again when deps change.');

challenges.title: Custom React Hooks: Encapsulating Logic
description: Custom hooks are one of React's most powerful features — they let you extract component logic into reusable functions. By convention, custom hooks always start with use.

// Custom hook: useLocalStorage import { useState } from 'react'; function useLocalStorage(key, initialValue) { const [storedValue, setStoredValue] = useState(() => { try { const item = window.localStorage.getItem(key); return item ? JSON.parse(item) : initialValue; } catch { return initialValue; } }); const setValue = (value) => { setStoredValue(value); localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(value)); }; return [storedValue, setValue]; } // Usage in any component: const [theme, setTheme] = useLocalStorage('theme', 'light');
Other common custom hooks: useFetch (data fetching + loading/error states), useDebounce (delayed search inputs), useWindowSize (responsive logic), useWebSocket (real-time connections).
Instructions

Write a function useDebounce (no React needed — pure JS) that takes a fn function and a delay in ms, and returns a new function that only calls fn after delay ms of inactivity. Calling the debounced function repeatedly should reset the timer each time.
challengeSeed: // Custom hook logic: debounce (used in search inputs, autocomplete, etc.)
// Set new timer that calls fn after delay
tests: var called = 0; var db = useDebounce(function() { called++; }, 50); db(); db(); db(); setTimeout(function() { assert(called === 1, 'message: Should only call fn once after rapid calls.'); }, 100);
assert(typeof useDebounce(function(){}, 100) === 'function', 'message: useDebounce should return a function.');

challenges.title: Next.js: Server-Side Rendering and the App Router
description: Next.js is the leading React framework in 2026, used by companies like Vercel, Netflix, TikTok, and Twitch. It extends React with: server-side rendering (SSR), static generation (SSG), the App Router, and React Server Components.

// Next.js App Router file: app/users/[id]/page.tsx import { notFound } from 'next/navigation'; // Server Component - runs on the server, no 'use client' needed async function UserPage({ params }: { params: { id: string } }) { const user = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/users/${params.id}`, { next: { revalidate: 3600 } // cache for 1 hour }).then(r => r.json()); if (!user) notFound(); return ( <main> <h1>{user.name}</h1> <p>{user.email}</p> </main> ); }

Key Next.js concepts for 2026: Server Components (default, run on server, zero JS to client), Client Components ('use client' directive, run in browser), Partial Prerendering (static shell + dynamic islands), and Server Actions (form submissions handled server-side).
Instructions

Write a function createRouter that takes a routes object mapping path patterns to handler functions, and returns a navigate(path) function. It should match exact paths and extract dynamic segments (e.g., /users/:id). Return null if no route matches.
challengeSeed: // Simulates Next.js App Router path matching
tests: var router = createRouter({ '/users/:id': function(p) { return 'user:' + p.id; }, '/about': function() { return 'about'; } }); assert(router('/about') === 'about', 'message: Exact route /about should match.');
assert(router('/users/42') === 'user:42', 'message: Dynamic route /users/:id should extract id=42.');
assert(router('/unknown') === null, 'message: Unknown path should return null.');
